The CSI 300 fell 8.5% in October, marking its worst monthly performance since early 2016.

China's technology-focused STAR 50 index has dropped around 40% from its June peak, wiping out approximately $480 billion in market value.

Fresh government support measures have failed to restore investor confidence, with AI concerns and economic weakness continuing to weigh on equities.

China’s stock market is facing one of its toughest periods in more than a decade as investors retreat from technology shares and reassess the country’s economic outlook. The CSI 300 has extended its losing streak to 12 consecutive weeks, falling 15% over the period and recording an 8.5% monthly decline in October. The latest selling has continued into November, despite Beijing announcing fresh measures to stabilise the market. Here are the three key factors driving the China stock market sell-off.

The global retreat from artificial intelligence stocks has become a major drag on Chinese equities. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the massive spending on AI infrastructure, semiconductors and computing capacity will generate sufficient returns.

🚨 MASSIVE CRASH IN CHINAOver CN¥1.58 TRILLION ($237B) wiped out from China's stock market as the SSE crashes -1.5%. pic.twitter.com/JMKx8lXDEr

China’s technology sector has been particularly vulnerable. The STAR 50 index, which tracks major technology companies listed on Shanghai’s STAR Market, has fallen around 40% from its late-June peak, erasing approximately $480 billion in market value.

The pressure intensified in October as selling spread across semiconductor and communications equipment companies. On October 30, the CSI 5G communications index dropped 6.2%, while optical module maker Eoptolink Technology plunged 14%. The STAR 50 also fell 5.5% during the session.

The weakness reflects growing concerns about AI valuations and the profitability of heavy capital expenditure. Investors are reassessing whether the expected growth in AI demand can justify the valuations built into technology stocks earlier this year.

Beyond the technology sell-off, persistent economic challenges are weighing on investor confidence. Weak domestic consumption and continued stress in the property sector have raised questions about the strength of China’s economic recovery.

The property market remains a significant concern, particularly as developers continue to face financial pressure. Recent reports that state-owned developer Zhuhai Huafa Group was seeking extensions on certain bank loans have added to worries about debt-related risks in the sector.

These concerns are creating an uncertain outlook for businesses and investors. Weak domestic demand can limit corporate revenue growth, while property-sector stress threatens to weigh on broader economic activity.

The CSI 300’s 8.5% October decline reflects the combination of these domestic challenges and the global technology sell-off. The index also lost 15% over 12 weeks, marking its longest losing streak on record.

Chinese authorities have stepped up efforts to stabilise the stock market following October’s sharp losses. However, the latest measures have yet to convince investors that a sustained recovery is underway.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) announced another round of swap operations that could provide more than 100 billion yuan in liquidity to financial institutions for stock purchases. It also made its share-buyback relending programme permanent and reduced the related interest rate from 1.25% to 1%.

Meanwhile, regulators encouraged major listed companies and leading technology firms to buy back shares. They also urged newly launched exchange-traded funds to build positions faster and are considering easing margin requirements to improve market liquidity.

The announcements initially supported a rebound, with the Shanghai Composite rising 1.1% on Monday, November 2. However, Chinese stocks reversed course in early trading on Tuesday, November 3, as investors continued selling technology and energy shares. The CSI 300 and Shanghai Composite both fell roughly 1% in early trade.

The outlook for Chinese equities will depend on whether policymakers can restore confidence and address the economic concerns driving the sell-off. Further liquidity support may help limit short-term volatility, but it may not be enough to reverse the broader downturn.

Investors will closely monitor AI companies’ earnings, domestic consumption and developments in the property sector for signs of improvement. A recovery in technology stocks could also help stabilise broader market sentiment.

For now, the CSI 300’s 8.5% October decline and the continued weakness in technology shares underline the challenges facing China’s equity market. Until investors see stronger earnings prospects and a more convincing economic recovery, the market could remain under pressure.

Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. A headline claiming that 1.8 billion XRP moved across the XRP Ledger within 24 hours has revived discussion of a network recovery. The figure hasn't been independently verified for a dated 24-hour period, so treat it as a reported claim, not confirmed evidence of a new trend.

The XRP Ledger handles payments, decentralized exchange transactions and tokenized assets. Payment volumes reflects the network activity, but the number needs context. Large transfers can be exchange custody movements, internal treasury operations or transfers between wallets controlled by the same entity.

None of that necessarily signals fresh investor demand or new capital entering the market.

Recent verified reporting shows why the distinction matters. One October snapshot had daily payment volume jumping to about 137.7 million XRP, still below its 30-day average of roughly 496 million.

Another October reading, around 363.3 million XRP, came with the same caution: a one-day rise did not establish a sustained recovery.

A reading near 1.8 billion XRP usually comes at the end of the week where most of the network activity occurs. The most likely outcome is always the same: high activity by Thursday and Friday and a tubmling on the weekend, with a recovery starting on Monday.

Other indicators help separate real adoption from a passing spike: active addresses, successful payment counts, decentralized-exchange trading, liquidity and how transaction sizes are distributed. Even high transaction counts can mislead when automated activity dominates, as recent investigations into small-value stablecoin payments on XRPL showed.

Network usage and XRP's market price are only indirectly related. More settlement activity doesn't guarantee higher token prices, and speculative buying can lift prices with no matching improvement in usage. Broader market conditions and exchange liquidity matter too.

A verified natural burst of XRP movement could mean renewed engagement with the network. A more convincing signal would be several consecutive days of stronger, widely distributed activity, backed by improving liquidity and sustained user demand, which rarely happens.

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

DISCOVER: Meme coin supercycle: Top performers this week

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

EXPLORE: CZ Tells Crypto Users to Be “Extra Careful” Online as PHP Vulnerabilities Hit the Code Behind 70% of Websites: Can a Hacked Site Drain Your Wallet?

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.

Crypto hacks and exploits have resulted in more than $11.4 billion in reported losses across 2025 and 2026.

Binance suffered a $6.36 billion breach, with attackers moving most funds within approximately 20 minutes across 10 blockchains.

Hackers also disrupted supermarket refrigeration systems across seven European countries.

The cryptocurrency industry has lost more than $11.4 billion to hacks and exploits across 2025 and 2026. The attacks have exposed weaknesses in exchange infrastructure, wallet security, and blockchain networks.

AI-powered attacks are spreading beyond crypto exchanges, with cyber incidents reported across at least 10 countries in the past 48 hours.

Data from DeFiLlama’s Hacks shows that the crypto industry recorded approximately $2.7 billion in losses during 2025. By 3 November 2026, reported losses had more than tripled to $8.776 billion across 328 incidents.

The February 2025 Bybit hack was one of the year’s biggest attacks, with around $1.5 billion in assets stolen.

However, 2026 has been far more costly, largely due to the 29 October Binance breach, which accounts for $6.36 billion in reported losses.

The Binance attack stands out because of how quickly hackers moved the stolen funds. Investigators traced them through around 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains in less than four days.

That is roughly one new wallet every 25 seconds.

However, the FBI linked the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking unit, which stole more than $6 billion in virtual assets and converted much of the funds into Ether.

Here are some of the largest crypto attacks reported over the past years.

Artificial intelligence is helping hackers carry out attacks in less time and with less effort.

Google researchers found that attackers built and launched an automated tool to steal login details in under six hours. Anthropic also reported AI-assisted attacks in which hackers completed breaches within two to three hours.

AI can help hackers find weak points in computer systems, create harmful software, steal passwords, and attack several targets at once. This means attacks that once needed large teams and days of preparation can now happen much faster with fewer people.

The cybersecurity concerns have also spread beyond digital assets. Hackers have targeted at least 10 countries in the past 48 hours, disrupting services and spreading false emergency alerts.

The UK has asked households to keep enough food and water for three days, while Japan recommends storing supplies for a full week.

At least 16 countries have issued similar advice.

#5290. Zcash (ZEC) Hits $1,280 Milestone but Fight Over Grant Money Sparks Whale Revolt

In late October 2026, Zcash (ZEC) reached a key milestone: the coin's price consolidated around $1,280, and its market capitalization hit $21.8 billion. However, the rapid rally was overshadowed by a sharp split within the community.

The trigger of the crisis was not a technical problem but a revolt of large investors over the targeted spending of capital.

Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the organization that distributes part of the miners' block reward, launched the Zcash Adoption Pool program. The fund directed grants toward the integration of vulnerable groups like refugees without access to banks.

The decision sparked protest from major players, since ZCG's charter allows it to distribute multimillion-dollar budgets bypassing the coinholder vote. The "whale" revolt moved into the practical realm: a major holder under the pseudonym "big z" publicly announced a full sell-off of his ZEC holdings.

According to him, the fund should finance cryptography, not political manifestos.

The local conflict quickly grew into a debate about the nature of decentralized money, which industry heavyweights joined. Developer Sean Bowe published a manifesto on the future of ZCG, in which he called for revising the fund's financing due to the anomalous surge in the ZEC price.

The initiative was unexpectedly supported by legendary investor Naval Ravikant, who laconically snapped that a $50 million cap is more than enough for community grants.

Meanwhile, the fund's activists continue to insist that private money is a "humanitarian imperative" and a public good.

However, Gemini exchange co-founder Tyler Winklevoss harshly challenged this thesis: a commercial network with transaction fees cannot be a public good. Winklevoss compared ZCG's actions to "taxation without representation" and called for leaving the development of Zcash to the free market.

The pressure on the price from the whales' coin sell-off coincided with the launch of direct ZEC deposits on the decentralized Rujira Network on October 29.

After failing to break above $1,390, the price settled in the $1,220–1,245 $range, still well below the all-time high of $1,698 set in late September. The fundamental dispute over who should control Zcash's millions remains open.

#5289. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

#5278. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

That hack set the floor. Bitcoin fell to $76,326 on October 30, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average), now at $76,512, and buyers have held above it for three days. Above, the 50-day EMA at $80,293 is now overhead, and $81,971, the October 29 high before the hack, caps the range.

#5275. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

#5272. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

#5270. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5269. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin halts transfers after $40M drained in ‘security incident’

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after identifying a security incident in one of its systems on November 2. The Brazilian crypto exchange later published destination wallet addresses to help trace assets connected to the incident.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze over 4.5 million USDT connected to the case. It is amongst other security incidents concerning crypto services, including Binance and old BTCPay Server software users, in the last few days.

Arkham separately valued wallets it attributed to the attacker at approximately $46 million on November 2. The tracked portfolio also included about $5.03 million in USDT, $3.02 million in USDC, $1.78 million in PEPE, $1.63 million in AAVE, and $1.46 million in PAX Gold.

Mercado Bitcoin responded quickly after discovering the breach; they claim it occurred overnight and that customers were financially unaffected while no data was lost.

They are investigating, tracking, and coordinating with the relevant authorities; deposits and withdrawals were stopped.

Following this, in a separate address, Mercado Bitcoin issued details of the addresses used on other blockchains for its transfers, including Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar, Tron, and their Ethereum-based/compatible services. It claimed the addresses were being published purely for tracing purposes.

The exchange also said it was working to restore operations safely and would keep customers informed through official channels. But there was no update about the reopening time or total financial impact.

Ardoino disclosed Tether’s intervention while sharing Mercado Bitcoin’s initial announcement.

“Tether froze more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident,” he wrote.

Tether can block transfers of its tokens at specific addresses, helping restrict their movement during an investigation. This was the second time in the last seven days that Tether has frozen funds associated with exploits. The latest was with Binance, when over $6 billion was exploited.

Ardoino’s announcement left the next steps for those frozen tokens unspecified, including their possible return to Mercado Bitcoin.

The incident follows Binance’s disclosure that attackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from its wallets on October 29. Binance began reopening withdrawals on November 1 and committed to covering the losses.

BTCPay Server issued an advisory of their own on November 2 after receiving reports that Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from wallets that stored the spending keys on impacted servers.

They found web servers from version 2.4.1 or less were targeted, and the bad actors were also able to exploit a vulnerability that they patched in August through another method.

BTCPay recommends moving to fresh servers and moving existing wallet/seed to the new one, since updating the affected software might leave an open door for hackers.

The team added that wallets with their spending keys held outside the servers, like most hardware wallets, were unaffected by these thefts. It continues investigating the scope of the incident fully.

Chainlink (LINK): Trading near $11.61, LINK is testing support around $11.00 and looks neutral to bearish in the short term.

Near Protocol (NEAR): Near $4.40, NEAR has a healthy longer-term chart but must hold $4.00–$4.20 to avoid a deeper correction.

Binance Coin (BNB): At about $714, BNB is defending the $690–$700 support zone with a neutral-to-bearish short-term outlook.

Chainlink is trading at about $11.61, well off its late-September peak near $15.75. On the daily chart, what was a strong bullish run has turned into a corrective consolidation, and right now the price is testing support.

LINK's bullish reversal came in August. It broke above its major moving averages and ran from roughly $8.00 to $15.75. The decline that followed has carved out lower highs and lower lows, and short-term momentum has deteriorated along the way.

The price is now under the shorter-term moving averages, which are bunched around $12.00–$12.60, so sellers still control the near-term trend. Still, LINK is holding above its 200-day moving average near $11.00, and as long as it does, the wider recovery stays intact.

The first support is $11.40–$11.50. Below that sits $11.00, a psychological level. If that gives way for good, the $10.40–$10.60 region comes into view; buyers showed up there recently.

Resistance starts near $12.00–$12.20, and the $12.50–$12.70 supply zone above it is the stronger barrier. Win those back, and a recovery toward $13.30 starts to look more likely.

Daily RSI is around 40–45, on the weak side of neutral. Buying momentum is subdued, but LINK isn't deeply oversold.

There was a sharp wick down toward $10.30 recently, and the price climbed back above $11.50 afterward. That could mean demand is soaking up the selling. One rejection candle doesn't confirm a reversal, though.

Short term, LINK looks neutral to bearish. Its next real move will probably be decided by the $11.00 support and the $12.20–$12.70 resistance zone.

NEAR Protocol trades near $4.40. It had a big rally off its August range of $1.60–$1.80, and even after the latest pullback the bigger structure still looks healthy. Short-term momentum is fading, though, so it may need to consolidate for a while before the next sustained leg up.

The breakout came in September. NEAR tore through several resistance levels and topped out around $6.00 in early October, on much heavier volume than usual, a sign that a lot of the market was taking part.

Since that peak it's been correcting: lower highs, and one test after another of the $4.20–$4.40 support region.

Right now NEAR is trading under its short-term moving averages, with resistance around $4.50–$4.80. The intermediate and long-term averages are still rising and sit well below the price, so the broader bullish structure doesn't look broken yet.

First support is $4.20–$4.30, the area that kept getting tested during the recent consolidation.

Under that, $4.00 is both a psychological and a technical support level. A decisive break there could expose $3.60–$3.70, roughly where the rising longer-period moving average sits.

On the upside, the first resistance is around $4.55–$4.70, then $4.90–$5.00. Break above $5.00 and hold, and the way could open toward $5.40, eventually $5.80–$6.00.

Volume exploded during the September breakout, so there was real buying behind it. It has cooled off since, as the price consolidates, and that points to less speculative interest.

The daily RSI has dropped back to around 40–45. Momentum is weaker, but there's no clear oversold signal. The latest bounce from roughly $4.00 shows buyers are still active lower down. It needs stronger follow-through to count for much. Getting back above $4.70, then $5.00, could restart the upward momentum, with $5.40–$5.80 as the target.

A confirmed daily close under $4.00 would make a deeper correction toward $3.60, and possibly $3.20, more likely.

NEAR's longer-term chart still looks healthy, but the short term is under corrective pressure. It has to hold $4.00–$4.20. A recovery to $4.70–$5.00 would be stronger evidence that buyers are taking back control.

Binance Coin is trading near $714 after a sizable pullback from its October highs around $800–$810. Short-term momentum on the daily chart is weakening, but the recovery that began in August hasn't been broken technically.

BNB broke out hard in late August and climbed from about $600 to $800. October was a different story, with a run of lower highs as buying pressure faded. The latest decline knocked BNB under its short-term moving averages at $730–$750, which tilts the near-term picture bearish.

Recently BNB tested $690–$700, where support lines up with the rising 200-day moving average, and bounced back to $714. Buyers look like they're defending that zone.

Resistance comes first at $730–$740 and then at $750–$760. A sustained recovery above $760 would improve the outlook and could open the way toward $780–$800.

On the way down, $700 is the first support, and $690 is the next. A confirmed daily close below $690 could speed up selling toward $670–$650.

The daily RSI is around 40–45. Momentum has weakened, but it isn't at extreme oversold levels, so a technical bounce is still possible. It would need stronger confirmation, though.

Bitcoin is trading near $77,871 after a sharp correction from its October peak around $87,000. Short-term momentum on the daily chart is getting worse, and BTC is closing in on a support zone that could decide where it goes next.

The August reversal was a strong one. BTC broke above its major moving averages and rallied from roughly $63,000 to $87,000. Then October brought a string of lower highs, as demand weakened and selling pressure built.

The latest drop took BTC below its short-term moving averages, which are concentrated around $80,500–$82,000. That area is now heavy overhead resistance.

The price recently dipped to about $76,000 before recovering toward $77,900. The rising 200-day moving average runs through the $76,000–$77,000 area, and another intermediate-term average is close by, so support is stacked there.

Immediate resistance is around $78,500–$79,000, then $80,500–$82,000. A sustained breakout above $82,000 would strengthen the case for a recovery and could bring $84,000–$86,000 into reach.

If BTC loses $76,000, the broader bullish structure weakens and a correction toward $74,000–$72,000 becomes more likely.

Daily RSI has dropped to about 40. That's bearish momentum, but it's getting near the levels where short relief rallies can start.

Selling volume has been high lately, so plenty of traders took part in the decline. That's why any return of buying demand needs to be confirmed.

Holding $76,000–$77,000 and taking back $80,500 could set off a recovery toward $82,000–$84,000.

A confirmed breakdown below $76,000 could speed up selling toward $74,000, possibly $72,000.

Bitcoin is testing a major long-term support region, and the short-term outlook is cautiously bearish. Defending $76,000 is what keeps the broader recovery intact. Reclaiming $82,000 would be a clearer sign that bullish momentum is back.

#5266. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

#5263. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

#5261. Horizen Holders Face November 4 Bridge Cutoff Before L3 Wind-Down

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Horizen users have a near-term operational deadline as the project winds down its layer-three network. Its official migration notice sets November 4 at 13:00 UTC as the bridge cutoff and directs holders to review the instructions for their particular assets.

The migration plan includes a later recovery process for certain remaining balances. That is not a universal guarantee for every token or wallet arrangement, making the difference between an ordinary withdrawal and a delayed recovery especially important.

A chain shutdown is different from a token being removed from an exchange. In the exchange case, the underlying network may continue to function normally. A network wind-down changes the infrastructure through which users can submit instructions and applications can update state.

That makes the location of an asset consequential. A token bearing the same name can exist in more than one environment, and the procedure for moving it depends on where the balance is actually recorded. A holder should not infer their position from a ticker in a portfolio tracker alone.

There is also a timing distinction between initiating an exit and receiving its result. Bridging can involve stages that finish after the first transaction. A successful submission is useful evidence, but the recipient-side balance and the bridge’s own status determine whether the transfer has completed.

Horizen says its later DAO return covers ZEN and qualifying ETH balances, while USDC.e is outside that process. The notice also flags special handling for smart-contract wallets and a minimum ETH balance threshold. Readers with affected holdings need the current official instructions rather than a generic assumption that all balances will be returned automatically.

These distinctions reflect an important feature of blockchain accounting: recognizing an address on two networks does not establish that the same kind of account exists on both. A simple wallet and a contract-controlled account can require different treatment when balances are reconstructed elsewhere.

Similarly, a bridged asset may be operated through infrastructure with obligations separate from those of the chain’s own project. A recovery programme can only make reliable promises about assets and processes within its stated scope.

The project attributes the accelerated transition to compatibility issues connected to Base’s Denim upgrade. Base’s published specification introduces a different block cadence and associated data changes, illustrating why infrastructure built on another chain must track its dependencies.

A layered system can borrow useful components and reduce development work. It can also inherit assumptions about how the underlying network behaves. When those assumptions change, the dependent service may need a migration rather than a routine version update.

This is a broader architectural lesson rather than evidence that all layer-three networks face the same outcome. The relevant question is which exact dependencies a system has and whether its operators can adapt them before an upstream change takes effect.

Moving activity to an established network can simplify the number of places where an ecosystem must maintain infrastructure. For users, however, the immediate benefit depends on successful balance transfers, working applications and clear communication about what happens to existing positions.

A staking interface being unavailable, for example, would not by itself establish that funds have disappeared. Equally, a roadmap promising future staking would not prove that a particular balance has already migrated. Transaction records and official recovery notices answer those different questions.

The November 4 cutoff is therefore the central fact for this week. The broader move to Base can be evaluated over time, but the asset-specific exit and recovery instructions deserve attention before the operating environment changes.

#5256. Devcon Opens in Mumbai This Week With Ethereum Builders Facing a Delivery Test

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

For people following Ethereum from the market side, the useful task is to separate ideas presented on a stage from changes that developers can actually test and users can eventually rely on. A conference creates a concentrated view of the work; it does not turn every proposal into a network commitment.

A protocol idea can be persuasive before its operational consequences are fully understood. It may improve one property, such as transaction handling, while adding costs elsewhere, such as data storage or the difficulty of running infrastructure.

The most informative technical presentations explain those trade-offs and offer a way for others to inspect the work. A specification, reproducible benchmark or test implementation gives outside developers something they can challenge. A performance target without those materials is harder to evaluate.

There is also a sequence between research, agreement on scope, client implementation, testing and activation. A talk about one stage should not be reported as completion of the next. This matters especially when short clips circulate without the qualifications that accompanied a presentation.

The Ethereum Foundation’s original Mumbai announcement described a gathering extending beyond protocol engineering. That wider participation matters because improvements in the underlying network only reach users through products, interfaces and operating processes.

A wallet team, for example, might need to turn a complex authorization into something a person can understand before signing. A payments developer needs to handle delayed confirmations and mistaken inputs. An institutional application needs to reconcile its blockchain records with the obligations in its legal agreements.

These are less dramatic achievements than a headline about speed, but they can determine whether an application is dependable. A credible demonstration should show what happens when the happy path breaks, including what a user sees and how the system recovers.

Open-source ecosystems distribute responsibility across people who do not all work for the same organization. A change can require cooperation among client teams, infrastructure operators, wallet developers and application maintainers, each with different constraints.

Bringing those groups together can shorten the distance between a proposed improvement and a clear understanding of its consequences. It can also expose disagreements that were easy to miss in a written thread. A resolved incompatibility may be a more useful outcome than another product announcement.

That kind of progress is difficult to measure through attendance figures. It becomes visible later, when documentation improves, implementations converge or a previously blocked integration starts working. The follow-up work is where a conference’s technical value is ultimately demonstrated.

Useful evidence will include published materials, specific engineering milestones and clearly identified owners for the next stage of a project. Readers should be able to distinguish a proposal seeking discussion from software ready for production.

For applications, the stronger indicators are working integrations and repeated use, alongside a credible explanation of costs and failure handling. A polished demonstration can establish that an idea is possible without proving that it works reliably at scale.

Devcon’s immediate importance is bringing Ethereum’s many development efforts into view at the same time. The longer-term story will depend on what survives scrutiny and becomes usable software. Neither the schedule nor a keynote provides a dependable forecast for ETH’s price.

#5255. XRP Final Move: Binance Empties Hacked Wallet of Last $101 Million

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

#5253. Solmate Discloses 1.26M SOL Custody Positions and Says It Has No Binance Exposure

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solmate Infrastructure has published a specific answer to a question facing crypto treasury companies after an exchange security incident: where are the assets held? In an October 30 disclosure, the company said it had no Binance accounts or exposure and identified the custodians holding its reported 1.26 million SOL.

The Form 6-K places those holdings with Kraken, Anchorage Digital or BitGo as of October 29. It is a company statement about custody at a particular time, rather than an independent audit of every position.

A corporate balance sheet can show exposure to a cryptocurrency without explaining the complete operating arrangement behind it. Investors also need to know who controls transactions, how transfers are approved and whether the company can access the assets when it needs them.

A treasury that plans to hold for years still faces shorter-term obligations. It may need cash for operating costs, collateral for financing or flexibility to respond to an unexpected event. Custody arrangements influence how quickly it can meet those needs.

Publishing the names of service providers improves the starting point for that analysis. It does not reveal the allocation among them, every account condition or the extent to which assets may be committed to another activity. Those details require additional disclosures.

During a security event, markets can struggle to distinguish companies directly affected from those sharing only a connection to the same asset class. A precise statement can reduce that uncertainty without making broader claims about the safety of the industry.

Solmate’s accompanying release says its validator infrastructure continued to operate normally. That addresses another part of the business: the systems participating in network operations, as distinct from where the treasury tokens are held.

The distinction is useful because an operating interruption and a custody loss are not interchangeable. A company could experience one without the other. Reporting them separately makes it easier to understand what an incident has actually changed.

Using more than one custodian can reduce dependence on a single operating platform, but it also creates work. A company must reconcile several records, maintain consistent authorization rules and understand the conditions for moving assets between accounts.

A simple example is a treasury policy requiring two approvals for a transfer. That rule must be enforceable wherever assets are held, rather than exist only in an internal document. Differences among service providers can become important when staff change or an urgent transfer is requested.

There is no evidence in this disclosure of a weakness in Solmate’s procedures. The point is that naming several providers is one component of risk management, not a complete description of it. Clear allocation and operational reporting would give shareholders a fuller view.

The number of SOL held is different from the cash value available to shareholders. That value changes with the token’s price and with the company’s wider liabilities, operating costs and financing structure.

A statement that assets are accounted for therefore cannot be translated into a guarantee about equity value. Nor does an unchanged custody position establish that tokens can be sold at a particular price without affecting execution.

Solmate’s filing is useful because it answers a bounded question with named counterparties and a dated balance. Investors assessing the company can combine that information with subsequent financial reports and operating disclosures, keeping asset safekeeping, liquidity and market exposure as separate parts of the analysis.

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.

#5248. Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Home » Cardano (ADA) » Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Cardano Foundation just opened the path for multi-billion tokenized shares on the mainstream Layer-1 network.

The Cardano Foundation has joined Switzerland’s Capital Markets and Technology Association, and the group has recognized Cardano’s CIP-0113 programmable token standard as equivalent to its own CMTAT framework for certifying tokenized shares.

The move advances regulated securities tokenization on the network at the same time ADA trades in a clear bearish structure and tests the $0.182 area.

The Foundation announced membership in CMTA on October 29. CMTA is the Swiss industry association that develops practical standards for issuing and managing securities on distributed ledgers.

Following the mainnet launch of CIP-0113 earlier in the month, CMTA’s Expert Committee treated a reviewed Cardano implementation of the standard as technically equivalent to CMTAT for equity securities.

NEW: Cardano Foundation joins CMTA, the Swiss entity "setting the standard for tokenized capital markets," alongside members including UBS, with $7T in AUM. CMTA has recognized $ADA's CIP-113 as "equivalent to the CMTAT—meaning issuers can use it to tokenize certifiable shares." pic.twitter.com/iqmz811b4U

Issuers that meet the deployment conditions can therefore use it to tokenize shares that are eligible for CMTA’s certification process.

CIP-0113 went live on Cardano’s (ADA) mainnet on October 7 without a hard fork. It lets issuers attach compliance rules.

KYC and AML checks, sanctions screening, freeze and seize powers, and transfer restrictions, directly to native Cardano tokens. The ledger enforces those rules on every transfer, mint, or burn.

The blokchain recognition is limited to tokenized shares (equity), does not extend to tokenized debt or Cardano’s base-layer infrastructure, and still requires each issuance to satisfy Swiss legal and technical checks.

Shortly after launch, Veridian, a digital-identity company spun out from the Foundation, tokenized its own shares as ledger-based securities under Switzerland’s DLT Act using the standard, becoming the first publicly identified issuer to do so.

While the institutional groundwork advances, ADA’s chart tells a different short-term story. On the 4-hour timeframe the token continues a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows. It has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is testing the $0.182 area.

A reclaim of $0.20 is widely viewed as the first requirement for any shift in near-term sentiment, with resistance levels clustered around 0.2004–0.2188.

Until that reclaim occurs, bears remain in control and further downside remains possible if buyers fail to defend the current zone.

The CMTA membership and CIP-0113 equivalence give Cardano a clearer route into regulated tokenized capital markets in Switzerland, where ledger-based securities already have a defined legal framework. MSB Intel says the opportunities are in the trillions.

The Cardano Foundation has joined CMTA, the Swiss body that sets tokenized securities standards, whose members include UBS, Pictet and Lombard Odier.UBS alone has $7.328T in invested assets.@Cardano pic.twitter.com/Vb4bVAac0X

No doubt, this is the kind of standard work that makes real-world assets (RWAs) practical rather than purely experimental.

#5247. Hashdex Adds Jane Street to Crypto Index ETF Authorized Participants

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Hashdex Nasdaq CME Crypto Index ETF has added Jane Street Capital to its list of authorized participants, according to an October 30 prospectus supplement. The document updates the firms able to participate in the product’s creation-and-redemption arrangements.

It is a market-structure development rather than a statement that Jane Street has made a long-term investment in the fund. That distinction matters when institutional names become attached to crypto products.

The SEC’s investor glossary describes authorized participants as financial institutions that enter contractual arrangements to buy and redeem creation units. Their role links the supply of a fund’s shares to activity in the market where those shares trade.

Most ordinary investors transact with another market participant through a brokerage account. An authorized participant operates at a different layer, dealing with larger blocks under the product’s documented procedures. The two activities support the same product but should not be confused.

A listed participant can make the infrastructure available without committing to create shares on every trading day. The appointment establishes a relationship and a permitted function. Actual activity depends on market conditions, commercial decisions and the rules governing the fund.

When demand for shares changes, the mechanisms for adjusting supply can influence how closely the traded price stays connected to underlying asset value. If those mechanisms are difficult or expensive to use, gaps can persist even when traders recognize them.

An additional participant may offer another route through which the market can respond. That can be useful if existing firms face their own balance-sheet constraints or operational interruptions. It does not guarantee narrower spreads, because execution also depends on the liquidity of the assets and the cost of hedging.

Consider a period when investors want to buy shares rapidly while underlying crypto markets are moving. A firm providing liquidity has to manage the price risk between the share transaction and the corresponding asset trade. Access to a creation process is necessary for some workflows, but it does not make that exposure disappear.

The Hashdex supplement also identifies an affiliation between Jane Street Capital and a crypto trading counterparty. Such disclosures help readers understand how firms involved in different parts of the process are connected.

The relevant analytical question is whether the structure can process orders reliably and on competitive terms. An institutional service relationship is not evidence that the firm expects the underlying cryptocurrencies to rise or that it will retain a directional position.

This is particularly important when reading fund-flow headlines. Net new shares, secondary-market turnover and an authorized-participant appointment describe different things. One concerns changes in product size, another concerns trading between holders, and the third concerns the operating network behind the product.

Useful follow-up measures include trading spreads, premiums or discounts and the consistency of creation and redemption activity. Those observations would show whether the expanded network changes the experience for investors.

They also need context. A wider spread during an unusually volatile session does not automatically establish that the fund’s structure has failed. Comparing conditions over time and against underlying-market liquidity is more informative than judging a single quote.

The October filing is a relatively small document with a meaningful operational purpose: it updates who can help connect the fund to its underlying markets. It adds a recognizable financial firm to that machinery, while leaving the investment case and future flow direction open to separate assessment.

#5244. WalletConnect Adds Stellar Payments as Bermuda Ticketing Rollout Targets 2027

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

WalletConnect is expanding payment access on Stellar while preparing a separate merchant rollout in Bermuda. Its October 29 announcement says WalletConnect Pay supports the network, with LOBSTR as the first live Stellar wallet.

The Bermuda initiative, developed with Penrose Partners, begins with ticketing platform Premier Tickets, or PTIX. That integration is expected in the second quarter of 2027, so wallet support available now should be distinguished from the planned merchant launch.

A payment interface needs to identify both the customer’s wallet and the transaction the merchant expects. Those tasks sound simple until an order expires, a customer changes devices or a transfer arrives after the checkout page has been closed.

For ticketing, the sequence is particularly important. The buyer wants confirmation that a seat has been secured; the organizer needs confidence that payment belongs to the correct order. A blockchain transaction hash does not, by itself, contain every detail of that commercial relationship.

A useful integration must connect payment status to inventory and customer support. Otherwise, a fast transfer can still create a slow service experience when the ticketing system cannot confidently match the money to the purchase.

The proposed PTIX arrangement sends customer funds to the event organizer’s wallet without the ticketing platform holding them. That design changes where money sits between the moment a customer pays and the moment the organizer can use it.

It can reduce the need for the platform to collect and subsequently distribute balances. It also requires careful handling of refunds, disputed orders and changes to an event. Those obligations do not disappear because the transfer takes a more direct route.

A cancelled concert offers a straightforward example. Returning a payment requires identifying the right recipient, confirming the amount and deciding which party is responsible for making the transfer. A well-designed service should make that process comprehensible to a customer who has no interest in the underlying network.

For an organizer, receiving a digital asset is useful only if it fits the business’s finances. The organizer needs to know how much usable value it has received, what costs apply and how the balance will pay suppliers or other expenses.

Some businesses may want to retain a token; others may prefer conversion into bank money. Those choices affect reconciliation and liquidity planning. The availability of a wallet connection does not establish that every merchant will make the same decision.

Payment records also need to remain useful after the event. A business must be able to connect sales, refunds and settlement to its own accounts. The more the system can handle these ordinary tasks predictably, the less specialist knowledge a merchant needs to accept the payment method.

The announced timeline gives observers a clear milestone: a functioning ticket purchase from a supported wallet, with a merchant receiving the expected funds and a buyer receiving the correct ticket. That is a more useful measure than the theoretical reach of a wallet network.

After launch, repeat use and the rate of failed or abandoned payments would help assess whether the option solves a real customer problem. Lower processing costs would matter if they survive the full journey, including conversion and support.

WalletConnect’s Stellar expansion opens a technical route, while the Bermuda project attempts to give that route a regular commercial purpose. The two developments fit together, but their different launch stages need to remain clear as the integration progresses.

Sui’s 40M TPS demonstration highlights blockchain’s push for speed, but its off-chain design raises questions about the actual figures.

Sui reached more than 40 million transactions per second in a demonstration highlighted by crypto commentator Linda, but those transactions did not run directly through its mainnet.

The demonstration, which she says took place at Sui Base Camp during Token2049 in early October, used “tunnels” to process activity off-chain before settling results on-chain. That makes it a different proposition from sustained mainnet throughput.

Linda connects the test to Sui chain push into AI-agent infrastructure. A Sui chain co-founder’s clip featured in the video describes plans for agent coordination, payments and auditable activity, alongside collaboration with Google.

The strategic ambition is clear; the demonstration alone does not establish production demand.

She describes potential private versions of Ethereum applications such as Uniswap and Aave, plus private swaps accessible through existing Solana wallets.

She also reports that Midnight has passed one million mainnet transactions and that daily transactions increased nearly 400-fold in a month.

The YouTube video does not supply the starting daily transaction count, limiting what that growth multiple says about sustained adoption.

Linda reports that Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade is live on mainnet beta, citing a reduction in finality from roughly 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. Those figures imply about an 85-fold improvement, rather than the approximately 40-fold increase stated in the narration.

For Cardano, she describes Leios as approaching rollout through the Dijkstra hard fork, with initial throughput expected at three to five times current levels and later improvements targeting 10–15 times. These remain forward-looking claims in the video, not demonstrated performance results.
