#5241. TRON became an early route for stolen Binance funds, Elliptic finds

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

TRON served as a major early route for moving assets stolen in the Binance hack, according to a November 2 investigation by Elliptic. The blockchain analytics firm traced funds spreading across roughly 7,700 TRON addresses before much of the activity shifted elsewhere.

Elliptic’s summary showed how the attackers moved on some of its assets during and after stablecoin issuers such as Tether froze billions of dollars. Elliptic estimated that about $3.24 billion in digital assets were still sitting at the addresses associated with the theft at around 07:00 UTC on November 2.

Binance reported approximately $6.3 billion stolen in the October 29 attack. The FBI subsequently attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

According to Elliptic’s investigation, the attackers swapped 234 million stolen USDT for TRX on SunSwap before Tether froze the remaining USDT on TRON.

A distribution wallet began breaking TRX into smaller chunk transfers on October 30. The funds travelled through thousands of different addresses and crossover bridges/services that exchange assets. ​

In total, $147M was seen leaving the TRON network, almost all of which left and reached the Ethereum network as ETH.

A total time of 51 hours was used, and a total of 1,113 transfers occurred from the time the distributing wallet came into service to its last transfer. The last transfer took place on 1 November at 05:33 UTC.

In another November 1 thread, analyst SomaXBT calculated that about $242 million was laundered in roughly two days using TRON-linked routes.

Over two-thirds of the amount was allocated to routes leaving TRON (194M versus 194M). An added $22M was an estimated amount of fees, trading costs, and price change.

In both investigations, the money was moved through several services, ending up in newly created wallets, adding another layer of extra steps investigators had to follow.

By early November 1, TRON activity had largely stopped, Elliptic said. Movement subsequently picked up on Ethereum, Solana, and other networks.

Early on November 2, all 233 million stolen XRP moved to six new addresses. Elliptic also identified about 28 BTC passing through transactions that combine multiple users’ Bitcoin, complicating tracing.

Only a tiny amount was likely cashed out, according to Elliptic, meaning it is still possible for exchanges and brokers to intercept because investigators will be following the assets.

#5239. Airtm and BVNK Plan Wallet Payments for Merchants in Emerging Markets

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Airtm and BVNK have announced an integration intended to let users spend wallet funds with participating retailers, extending digital-dollar services beyond receiving and holding money. The October 29 joint announcement links Airtm Connect with BVNK’s stablecoin-payment infrastructure and says the integration will use Stellar.

The commercial objective is straightforward: a balance becomes more useful if its owner can spend it without repeatedly moving through disconnected services. Delivering that convenience requires the entire payment process to work, including the steps outside the blockchain.

A customer who receives digital dollars may still need to pay merchants using a different system. Each conversion or transfer can introduce a fee, a delay and another opportunity to select the wrong details.

Connecting a wallet directly to a merchant payment flow could remove some of that handling. The user would begin with the balance they already possess, rather than first preparing money in a separate account solely for the purchase.

The improvement depends on whether the customer can understand the final cost before confirming. A low network fee is only one element. Exchange rates, payment-provider charges and any conversion into the merchant’s chosen settlement currency also determine what the purchase actually costs.

A payment option is difficult to use regularly if adding money to the wallet is unreliable. Conversely, convenient funding has limited value if the customer cannot use the resulting balance where they shop.

The partnership combines providers working at different parts of that chain. The implication is a chance to make funding, wallet access and merchant acceptance feel like one service, even when multiple organizations perform the underlying work.

Consider someone paid by an overseas customer who then purchases a subscription. A coherent flow should preserve enough information to show the incoming payment, the available balance, the purchase and any refund. If the customer must reconstruct those records across several interfaces, some of the convenience has been lost.

A successful network transaction and a completed retail order are related, but they are not identical. The merchant needs to know that the transfer corresponds to a valid order and meets its settlement requirements before delivering the product.

That creates several possible intermediate states. A customer may approve a payment after the original quote expires. A merchant may cancel an order while a transfer is processing. A service may need to reverse the commercial transaction even though the blockchain transfer itself cannot simply be deleted.

These are normal payment-system problems rather than reasons to dismiss the model. The quality of an integration shows in how consistently it handles them, especially for users who cannot afford to wait through a lengthy support process to recover a modest balance.

The announcement establishes a planned route to participating retailers. It does not imply that every merchant connected to a broader financial network will immediately accept an Airtm wallet payment.

Practical evidence would include which countries and merchants are enabled, the available funding methods and the time between payment approval and a usable settlement balance. Successful repeat purchases would say more about adoption than the number of people who could theoretically access the service.

For stablecoin markets, this is a useful test of whether digital-dollar infrastructure can support ordinary spending without adding complexity for the customer. Airtm and BVNK have described the connection they want to build. Its value will come from how well funding, checkout and after-sales support fit together once people use it.

Less than 48 hours remain before the U.S. midterm elections.

This is the first big election to follow the 2024 presidential elections that sent the crypto market into a frenzy after pro-crypto Donald Trump won.

But now that the odds of a Democratic sweep of the midterms are over 73%, it brings up the question whether crypto will do the same if the Republicans fall short.

The stakes are higher for Ripple. As the chart below shows, XRP had the most explosive rally of the post-election period in 2024. It rose over 280% in November. The key takeaway? November has historically been XRP’s strongest month, with average returns above 80%.

That naturally puts Ripple [XRP] under the spotlight ahead of the upcoming elections.

Interestingly, XRPL is exhibiting a balanced picture on-chain, as the number of transactions is currently hovering around 3.29 million, while the volume of transactions is sitting at just under $2.32 billion. Active addresses are also an important metric to monitor. While transactions are being processed, the adoption of users needs to increase.

In essence, Ripple has been relatively quiet on-chain. This raises a key question: Can XRP’s ongoing supply squeeze provide enough bullish pressure to fuel a breakout, even as on-chain demand remains subdued?

Ripple kicked off November with its scheduled 1 billion XRP escrow unlock.

However, shortly after, 700 million were re-locked, meaning that the net amount being released is actually 300 million. It’s common for a large amount of tokens to be locked back into escrow each month. In the past year, Ripple has unlocked 12 billion XRP but has also locked 8.4 billion.

This means that the real amount of supply coming into the market is far smaller than the 1 billion figure.

As can be seen in the post below, Ripple has placed 700 million XRP back in escrow through three transactions. Simply put, this means that these tokens cannot be released into the market immediately.

After the 1 billion XRP was unlocked, there are now just 300 million XRP available outside of escrow. This means less supply pressure.

Against this backdrop, XRP’s on-chain signals start to matter.

According to SoSoValue, ETFs have so far seen an impressive increase of $4.32 million in weekly inflows, surpassing last week’s $4.25 million, with the best weekly inflows since mid-September.

Combined with recent whale activity, the fact that XRP has been able to stay above $1.20 suggests it could be in an early accumulation phase.

With the midterm elections approaching, this setup puts XRP on the watchlist for a potential post-election rally, provided broader market sentiment turns bullish.

Ripple locked 700 million of the 1 billion unlocked XRP back into escrow. In turn, leaving only 300 million in net new supply.

Home » Trendsetter News » HashPack Adds HBAR Tokenized Stock Without LP Reliance

HashPack users can now access tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX using HBAR or Hedera’s wrapped USDC version.

HashPack users can now buy tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX without relying on liquidity pools on Hedera, according to CEO and co-founder May. Speaking with the host about the wallet’s latest upgrades, she described an integration that lets users pay with HBAR or Hedera USDC while accessing liquidity outside the network.

That distinction matters for larger trades. Assets traded through shallow pools can suffer significant price slippage; May said the SODAX integration avoids depending on locally supplied liquidity to execute purchases.

According to May, buyers receive an HTS token representing a Robinhood stock token issued on Robinhood Chain. She said SODAX maintains the one-to-one relationship, giving users exposure to the underlying asset’s price without requiring another wallet or a manual move to another blockchain.

“You’re not relying on liquidity that exists on the network,” she said. Previously, most assets available to trade through HashPack depended on SaucerSwap pools, apart from token-launch platforms that subsequently created pools there.

May also described dividends as being reinvested into the same stock rather than distributed as cash, qualifying that explanation with “as far as I know.”

The interview did not establish the products’ legal ownership rights, redemption terms or geographic restrictions; details investors would need before treating them as interchangeable with brokerage-held shares.

She sees potential for lending and borrowing against tokenized stocks, although the discussion did not establish that those functions are available inside HashPack.

The stock integration accompanies HashPack’s “Portfolio” redesign, which adds a customizable homepage and bottom-opening navigation dock. May said most users access the wallet on mobile, and its growing collection of swaps, staking options and NFT integrations had made features harder to find.

Enterprise integrations remain a slower prospect. HashPack has ongoing discussions, May said, but nothing particularly exciting to flag for the short term; she suggested developments could emerge over 12 to 24 months.

#5235. Taurus Adds Stellar Smart-Contract Assets to Institutional Custody and Issuance

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Taurus has expanded its Stellar integration to support smart-contract-based assets, giving institutional clients a broader set of custody and issuance functions. The company said on October 29 that the capabilities are live through Taurus-PROTECT and Taurus-CAPITAL.

The official announcement describes an extension of existing Stellar support rather than a newly announced fund or security. The change matters because institutions need more than a place to store a token once it has been created.

Safekeeping is often described as protecting private keys. For an institution, a useful custody system must also govern what those keys are allowed to authorize, who can request an action and which approvals are needed before it proceeds.

A simple transfer and a smart-contract interaction can carry different consequences. An instruction may change an allowance, invoke a contract function or alter how an asset can be handled. The approving person needs enough information to understand that consequence before a signature is produced.

This creates a practical reason to integrate smart-contract support into the tools an institution already uses. A separate experimental interface may be technically capable of sending an instruction while sitting outside the organization’s normal operating controls.

Creating a tokenized instrument requires decisions about the rights it represents and the actions permitted after issuance. Depending on the instrument, those may include transfers, subscriptions, redemptions or changes governed by the issuer’s rules.

Taurus says the release supports several Stellar token models, including structures intended for regulated assets. That flexibility can help an institution match its technical implementation to the instrument it wants to offer, rather than treating every token as economically identical.

It also raises an integration question: can the legal and operational records remain consistent with the contract state? A token should not appear transferable in an application when the issuer’s rules prohibit the intended recipient from holding it.

A financial firm considering another blockchain faces costs beyond deploying a contract. Staff need familiar approval processes, finance teams need reports and operations teams need a procedure for handling failed instructions.

Reusing an established custody and issuance interface may reduce the number of new systems those teams must learn. It can also make oversight more consistent across networks, provided the interface still exposes the differences that matter.

For example, an operations dashboard should not imply that two assets have identical settlement behaviour simply because they appear in neighbouring rows. Network-specific requirements, contract permissions and servicing obligations need to remain visible where they affect decisions.

The release establishes that clients have more infrastructure options on Stellar. The next evidence of adoption would be institutions using those capabilities for named instruments with clearly explained ownership and transfer arrangements.

There is a difference between supporting a contract standard and completing a reliable asset-servicing process. A production service must handle routine transactions, unusual requests and the reconciliation that follows. Its value lies in reducing the effort required to do those jobs correctly.

For Stellar, the potential benefit is a wider route for institutional asset activity. For Taurus clients, it is the ability to consider another network without rebuilding every surrounding control. Neither outcome should be measured simply by the number of token standards listed in a release.

The more revealing test is whether an issuer can take an asset from creation through ongoing management and eventual redemption using a coherent set of records. Taurus’s announcement expands the available toolkit for that work; actual products and operating results will show how effectively it is used.

#5231. Ripple and Water.org Expand Stablecoin Work as Aid Payments Move Faster

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Ripple and Water.org are expanding a partnership that applies payment and stablecoin infrastructure to water and sanitation financing. Ripple’s late-October announcement describes wider use of Ripple Payments, RLUSD and wallet services across the nonprofit’s operations.

The company reports that earlier work moved more than $3.2 million across four markets, with same-day settlement in Mexico and Brazil replacing waits of two to three days. Those are partner-reported operational results, not an independent measure of every programme outcome.

Water.org’s WaterCredit programme works with local financial institutions to make small loans for household water and sanitation improvements. Its role includes supporting partners with resources and expertise, while those institutions provide the financing.

That model makes the movement of capital an important operational link. Money may originate in one country, pass through an international funding arrangement and ultimately support a local loan used to install a tap, toilet or other improvement.

Speed in one part of that chain can help, particularly when it reduces idle balances or uncertainty over when funds will arrive. It cannot substitute for sound lending, reliable local contractors or a household’s ability to use the completed infrastructure.

A cross-border transfer can involve several forms of cost: bank charges, currency conversion, the time staff spend reconciling records and the cash held while a payment is pending. A change in infrastructure may improve some of those elements without changing all of them.

The useful comparison is therefore the amount and timing of usable money at the destination. A token arriving quickly is not the same as a local lender having the currency and information needed to disburse a loan.

For example, a settlement message that arrives over a weekend may still require a local conversion or approval process. Measuring that whole sequence would show whether continuous digital settlement translates into a practical advantage for the programme.

Adding a stablecoin gives an organization another way to hold and transfer a claim denominated in dollars. It also creates tasks around access permissions, reconciliation and the conditions for converting the balance into another form of money.

A nonprofit’s finance team needs to connect those balances to grants, programme budgets and expenditure records. The technology is most useful when it fits that discipline, rather than requiring the organization to maintain a separate set of unexplained onchain transactions.

Custody and wallet services can form part of that operating model. The important question is who is allowed to move funds and how the organization checks that an instruction matches an approved purpose. Faster settlement increases the value of getting those controls right before execution.

Payment completion times and processing costs show whether the financial infrastructure works more efficiently. Household access to safe water and sanitation shows whether the wider programme achieves its purpose. Both are relevant, but one should not be used as an automatic proxy for the other.

A credible expansion would report the relationship between the two: whether lower costs leave more funding available, whether quicker transfers improve loan availability and whether local delivery remains reliable as the programme grows.

For crypto, this is an adoption story with a concrete use for moving money, rather than a claim that a token’s price must benefit. The partnership gives Ripple and Water.org a setting in which payment infrastructure can be assessed against a practical objective. The strongest results will be those that trace an operational improvement through to the people the financing is intended to reach.

Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

#5229. 5 Best AI Crypto Trading Bots

Compare five AI crypto trading bots by automation features, strategy tools, supported exchanges, ease of use, and key limitations.

AI crypto trading bots help traders automate strategies, analyze market data, and manage trade execution without monitoring charts around the clock. However, not every crypto trading bot marketed as AI-powered uses artificial intelligence to make trading decisions. Some platforms rely primarily on predefined rules, while others use AI to build strategies, interpret market conditions, or configure automated trading systems.

The best AI crypto trading bot depends on what you need: strategy automation, AI-assisted decision-making, beginner-friendly controls, or trading across multiple exchanges. This guide compares five platforms based on their available features, intended use cases, and practical limitations.

We looked at each platform’s automation features, strategy tools, backtesting options, supported exchanges, ease of use, pricing, and risk-management features. We also checked the information against each platform’s official website. Our picks are based on the features each bot offers and who it may suit best, rather than independently tested trading results. Keep in mind that features, fees, and exchange support can change over time.

3Commas is a crypto trading platform that combines automated bots with tools for managing and executing trades. It is widely used for multi-exchange order execution and parameter-driven  3Commas AI Trading Bot setups.

Its features include Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) bots, grid bots, signal-based trading, and SmartTrade order management.

The platform also offers an AI trading assistant that lets users describe a strategy in natural language. According to 3Commas, the assistant can configure a bot, run a backtest using historical market data, and prepare the strategy for launch.

Limitation: Bot capacity on the entry plan is small, and higher limits require Pro or Expert. Backtests also cannot fully reproduce future market conditions, slippage, liquidity constraints, or unexpected volatility.

3Commas is worth considering for traders who want to automate established trading strategies while retaining control over entry conditions, position sizing, and exits. It is particularly relevant to users who already understand concepts such as DCA, grid trading, and technical indicators.

Cryptohopper is a cloud-based engine that combines automated crypto trading with strategy-building, backtesting, and AI-assisted tools.

Its AI Strategy Designer helps traders choose strategies, signal providers, and TradingView alerts based on current market conditions. However, access depends on the subscription plan, so it’s worth checking the requirements before signing up.

Cryptohopper also has Cryptohopper.AI, a separate tool that lets users create trading bots and other trading tools simply by describing what they want in plain language. Although both use AI, they serve different purposes and shouldn’t be confused with each other.

Limitation: Access to certain AI features depends on the product and subscription tier. AI-generated strategies still require testing and monitoring before live deployment.

Cryptohopper trading bot suits traders who want to experiment with different strategies and automate their selection or execution. It is also relevant to users interested in building customized crypto trading tools without writing all the code themselves.

Pionex is a cryptocurrency exchange with AI trading bots built directly into its platform. Unlike third-party automation services that require users to connect exchange accounts, Pionex integrates bot functionality into the exchange itself.

Pionex offers 16 bots, including Grid Trading, Infinity Grid, Trailing Buy/Sell, Rebalancing, and Spot-Futures Arbitrage bots. The options also include PionexGPT, an AI-related feature that allows users to write custom trading strategies using natural language prompts.

Limitations:  Funds are held on the Pionex exchange rather than on an exchange you already use, so the AI trading bots cannot be applied to other exchanges.

Pionex is a good option for beginners who want to try automated trading without paying for a separate bot service or connecting to another exchange. It can also be useful for experienced traders who prefer to manage everything on one platform.

Coinrule focuses on rule-based crypto trading automation. Users can create strategies by setting simple rules rather than building a trading system entirely from scratch.

With features like Coinrule AI Cloud, users can also use plain language to create trading strategies, get help setting them up, test them against historical data, and connect with compatible AI assistants.

Limitation: Rule-based automation follows its configured conditions; it does not inherently understand market context or predict future prices. It doesn’t provide the level of mathematical detail and precise order book analysis that professional institutional traders need.

Coinrule is suitable for traders who know what conditions they want to trade but do not want to write the underlying code. It is also useful for users who want to test systematic strategies before connecting them to live trading.

Bitsgap is a crypto trading platform that brings everything together in one place, including automated crypto AI trading bots, portfolio management, analytics, and exchange connections. It offers different trading bots, such as Grid and DCA, to help users automate their strategies. Its AI Assistant also helps users configure their trading setups.

With support for multiple crypto exchanges, Bitsgap lets users manage their trading activities through a single interface.

Limitation: Futures bots are not available on the Basic plan.Exchange support and available features vary.

Bitsgap is a good option for traders who use multiple exchanges and want to manage their trading bots in one place. Its automation tools and analytics also make it easier to track strategies and monitor performance.

The best AI crypto trading bot is the one whose capabilities match your trading approach, not necessarily the one with the most AI features.

Before choosing a platform, compare these factors:

AI crypto trading bots can automate execution and reduce the need for constant manual monitoring, but profitability is never guaranteed. Results depend on strategy design, market conditions, execution costs, liquidity, and risk management.

Historical backtests are useful for evaluating a strategy, but they do not establish that it will perform similarly in live markets. Traders should test bots in simulation where possible, start with limited exposure, and monitor performance after deployment.

An AI label alone is not evidence of a trading advantage. Before selecting a bot, establish what the AI actually does, how trades are triggered, and how losses are managed.

The answer depends on the use case. Pionex requires no API setup or subscription, 3Commas builds bots from plain-English prompts, Bitsgap covers 17+ exchanges, and Cryptohopper offers a strategy marketplace.

No profitability can be assumed. Results depend on settings, fees, and market conditions, and losses are possible.

It depends on the platform. 3Commas states it is non-custodial and connects through APIs, while Pionex operates as an exchange where funds are deposited.

XRP’s latest withdrawal surge reflects more than routine whale activity, as Binance’s reported security breach triggered significant movements across exchanges.

At the end of October, there was a sharp increase in big XRP transfers. During that period, roughly 283 million XRP were withdrawn from Binance. Whales’ net outflows reached 226 million.

Investigators concluded that around 233 million XRP were sent to external accounts using compromised Binance accounts. Afterward, Binance suspended withdrawals, resulting in a 94.8% drop in large XRP withdrawals to 14.7 million on the 30th of October.

Withdrawals increased back up to 80 million XRP on the 1st of November after withdrawals started again

If these large XRP are moved off of exchanges, they can potentially decrease the amount of XRP being held on exchanges and therefore limit short-term selling pressure. The fact that the hackers used compromised accounts complicates the indication of accumulation.

Thus, XRP may continue to be volatile due to the uncertain nature of the recent hacks.

The movement of hack-linked funds has added another layer of uncertainty to Binance’s recovery efforts.

In one instance, a wallet labeled “Binance Hack 2026” transferred 40 million XRP worth approximately $50.49 million to another anonymous account also labeled “Binance Hack 2026.”

This implies that instead of simply being left inactive in their respective initial wallets, the hackers’ ill-gotten gains are actively being utilized and transferred on chain. However, the transfer does not confirm liquidation or movement into an exchange.

Instead, it adds more confusion regarding what exactly the hacker will do with the assets next, whether they plan to sell them, consolidate their stash, or set up future transfers.

Therefore, monitoring where the recipient wallet ultimately ends up and follows through on each of its subsequent transactions is crucial.

Ultimately, any movement toward exchange-linked addresses could increase concerns about potential selling pressure and recovery efforts.

Despite growing fears that the hack-related movements may result in a decrease in XRP’s exchange liquidity, institutional flows tell a more resilient story. Weekly inflows into XRP spot ETFs totaled $4.32 million by the end of October.

These inflows came after a one-week withdrawal of $1.84 million from those same ETFs occurred on the 16 of October. It appears that investors continued adding capital to these investment products regardless of ongoing market issues and uncertainty surrounding XRP.

Prior to this period of inflow, the funds investing in these ETFs attracted $11.31 million during the week ending on the 9th of October. As such, cumulative net inflows into these investment vehicles reached $1.81 billion.

However, total net assets declined from $1.66 billion to $1.42 billion throughout October as XRP’s market value weakened. This contrast suggests fresh institutional buying has not fully offset valuation losses, leaving ETF demand supportive but insufficient to reverse broader price pressure.

Ripple saw hack-linked Binance outflows surge, raising concerns over stolen funds and potential selling pressure.

XRP ETFs sustained inflows, but falling net assets highlight weak price performance.

#5227. SAT Japan Adds USDT and USDC Payments With Dollar Settlement Through Triple-A

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Japanese vehicle exporter SAT Japan has added a stablecoin payment route through Triple-A, targeting the cross-border transfers involved in buying a car from overseas. The October 29 announcement says eligible customers can use USDT and USDC while the exporter receives settlement in US dollars.

The arrangement puts the payment processor between the buyer’s digital asset and the seller’s preferred currency. SAT Japan does not need to hold or manage the stablecoins itself, according to the companies.

A vehicle purchase involves more than clicking a checkout button. The seller needs to connect a substantial incoming payment to a specific vehicle and buyer, while the customer wants confidence that the transfer has arrived before shipping arrangements proceed.

Cross-border banking can add uncertainty about fees, intermediary deductions and processing times. A stablecoin route offers a different way to move value, but its commercial usefulness depends on the clarity of the complete transaction.

The buyer needs to know which asset and network are accepted, how long a quoted amount remains valid and when the seller will treat the invoice as paid. A transfer that reaches the wrong address or uses an unsupported network is not rescued by the fact that the token is designed to track a dollar.

Receiving dollars allows the exporter to separate customer payment choice from the currency it uses for accounting and operations. That is a different proposition from a business deciding to accumulate cryptocurrency on its balance sheet.

The processor’s role is central to that separation. It must recognize the payment, carry out the required checks and deliver the agreed settlement. The blockchain leg can be rapid while the overall process still includes compliance and banking steps.

This makes the service closer to an alternative payment rail than a bet on token prices. The seller’s objective is to receive a usable, reconciled payment for a vehicle. The buyer’s objective is to complete the purchase using money they can access.

Changing the payment method does not establish the condition of a vehicle, its shipping timetable or whether it meets the rules in the destination country. Those remain parts of the purchase agreement and import process.

A payment confirmation can prove that funds moved, but it cannot by itself prove that the promised goods were delivered. Buyers and sellers still need clear documentation identifying the vehicle, the agreed price and the responsibilities around transport and cancellation.

Refund handling is another practical question. If a purchase cannot proceed, the parties need to know whether a refund will be made in bank money or a digital asset, how any conversion is priced and who bears the associated charges. Those details should be understandable before a high-value transfer is sent.

The most revealing metrics would be the number of customers choosing the new option, the time to confirmed settlement and the total cost compared with the alternatives available to those same buyers.

Geography will matter. A method that improves a particular corridor may offer little advantage where bank transfers are already cheap and predictable. Eligibility and local access also determine whether the option is genuinely convenient for an overseas customer.

SAT Japan and Triple-A have identified a plausible use case for stablecoins: moving substantial payments across borders while allowing a conventional merchant to settle in a familiar currency. The test is whether the integration reduces uncertainty in actual purchases, including exceptions and refunds, rather than simply adding another logo to the payment page.

#5225. Chrome Can Now Pull Details From Your Gmail to Fill Out Web Forms

Chrome Can Now Pull Details From Your Gmail to Fill Out Web Forms

Google’s Chrome browser can now pull personal details from your Gmail inbox to fill out online forms for you, the company said in its announcement on Wednesday.

The update, called “enhanced autofill,” suggests order numbers, tracking information, and flight bookings when a form asks for them, wrote Amanda Lim, a Chrome product manager, in the announcement. Autofill is the browser tool that types in details like your name and address so you don’t have to.

It runs on Gemini, Google’s AI assistant, through a feature called Personal Intelligence, which lets Gemini draw on connected apps such as Gmail and Google Photos to tailor its answers to your own life. It is rolling out to Gemini in Chrome users who have Personal Intelligence turned on, on desktop, Android and iOS, starting in the U.S.

Google’s post names only those three kinds of data as coming from Gmail. Credit card numbers and addresses are part of Chrome’s standard autofill, which fills them from details you have saved in the browser, and the announcement does not say the new feature pulls them out of your inbox.

“You can manage whether enhanced autofill is enabled and what it can access via your Chrome settings,” Lim wrote. “As always, sensitive data is encrypted and you remain in control.”

Encryption scrambles data so only Google and other authorized parties can read it, though the post does not explain how that applies to the Gmail content Chrome reads or what it scans.

Users choose whether to connect their apps and can switch the connections off at any time, the post says, though Google does train on limited information, such as specific prompts and the model’s responses.

In November, users pushed back on a Smart Features setting that let Gemini analyze emails and calendars unless they opted out, and Google said it had not changed its underlying data-handling practices.

Chrome also dropped a line from its settings saying on-device AI, meaning models that run on your own computer rather than Google’s servers, works without sending data to Google servers. Google said the wording change did not reflect a change in how it handles on-device AI.

The rollout began Wednesday in the U.S. on desktop, Android and iOS, and Google’s announcement gives no date for other countries

BEAM’s rally was mainly driven by supply shock. Historically, such upside moves have been short-lived, and the current rally was no different.

Investors who chased this rally have since turned bearish and begun exiting their positions. On the Spot side, sell volume exceeded buy volume for the first time in four days, rising to 508 million while sell volume fell to 459 million.

On the derivatives side, investors were even more bearish. According to CoinGlass data, Open Interest plunged 25% to $14.4 million, while the derivatives volume fell 22% to $75 million.

Falling OI alongside the volume suggested reduced market participation while traders closed their positions. This suggested a shift in sentiment toward risk-off.

In doing so, BEAM will likely drop to $0.0033. To invalidate this bearish outlook, the altcoin needs to reclaim $0.005 and see a close above $0.0057.

#5223. DMG Says Client Assets Are Secure and Highlights Layered Transaction Controls

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

DMG Blockchain Solutions said on October 31 that it and its affiliates had not been affected by the Binance security incident and that client assets remained secure. The company described restricted access, separated duties and multiple approval levels intended to prevent one compromised device from authorizing an unauthorized transaction.

The issuer statement brings two distinct questions into view: where a business has exposure, and how it controls the movement of assets.

A company reporting that it was unaffected gives investors information about its assessment of a particular event. That is useful when a disruption at one service prompts questions about losses or interrupted access elsewhere.

The statement should still be read for what it establishes. Being unaffected does not, by itself, disclose every counterparty balance, contractual relationship or potential future dependency. It is possible for a business to have a commercial relationship with a service without suffering a loss from a specific incident.

That distinction avoids turning an asset-safety announcement into a claim of zero exposure that the company did not make. It also helps investors ask more precise follow-up questions about custody arrangements, operating balances and the services needed to keep transactions moving.

The security principle behind divided responsibilities is straightforward: a person or device able to prepare an action need not also have enough authority to complete it. The NIST glossary describes separation of duty as restricting the privileges available to any one user, including through a two-person control.

In a financial workflow, that can mean separating a proposed transfer from the independent checks that authorize it. The purpose is to make an attacker overcome more than one barrier before assets move.

The quality of the separation matters more than the number of approval prompts on a screen. Two approvals offer less independence if both depend on the same compromised credentials, device or source of transaction information. Reviewers need a trustworthy basis for checking the destination and intended amount.

These are general design considerations, not findings about a weakness in DMG’s systems. The public statement describes the company’s approach without publishing the detailed configuration needed for an outside technical assessment.

A description of a control explains what it is intended to prevent. Evidence that the control operates consistently would address a different issue: whether actual access rights, approval records and exception handling match that design.

For a client or institutional counterparty, the appropriate evidence can depend on the service. A review might examine who can change permissions, how unusual transfers are escalated and what happens when an approver is unavailable. The objective is to understand the functioning process, including its less convenient moments.

A public reassurance should therefore sit alongside the continuing work of oversight. It can communicate an incident assessment promptly without substituting for the deeper information that a contractual relationship may require.

Preventing an unauthorized transfer is one part of dependable asset management. A business also needs a way to complete legitimate activity when a device fails, an employee is absent or an external service becomes unavailable.

That creates a practical balance. Recovery arrangements must restore authorized operations without quietly removing the protections that make the system resilient. An emergency path that bypasses every ordinary control would change the security assessment substantially.

DMG’s update supplies a dated company position on asset safety and the control philosophy behind its transaction process. For investors, the useful distinction is between the reported outcome of this incident and the continuing evidence needed to assess custody, approvals and operational continuity over time.

#5221. Coinbase Swings to $719 Million Q3 Profit on Crypto Gains

Coinbase Swings to $719 Million Q3 Profit on Crypto Gains

Coinbase is back in the black, though much of that came from the crypto on its own balance sheet.

The exchange reported third-quarter net income of $719 million, or $2.51 per diluted share, on Thursday, ending a two-quarter losing streak. Analysts had expected a loss of 15 cents per share, according to Zacks. But about $715 million of the profit came from gains on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment. Excluding those and other investment gains, adjusted net income was $78 million.

Total revenue came in at $1.22 billion, in line with expectations, flat from the second quarter and down 35% from a year earlier. Transaction revenue slipped 1% to $590 million but beat the roughly $527 million analysts expected, as crypto volatility sank to multiyear lows and trading volume across the market fell.

The standout was prediction markets, which crossed $200 million in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase’s history, the company said.

Daily traders grew more than 60% from the prior quarter, and revenue has compounded 82% per quarter since launch. CEO Brian Armstrong said the product kept “growing even through slower sports months.”

“Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility,” CFO Alesia Haas said.

Coinbase also cut its 2026 adjusted expense guidance by another $100 million at the midpoint, to between $4.15 billion and $4.3 billion, following cost reductions in May. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 60% from the prior quarter to $333 million. Through Oct. 25, fourth-quarter transaction revenue stood at about $165 million.

The positive results follow two consecutive losing quarters. Coinbase posted a $394 million loss in the first quarter and missed estimates in the second as trading activity slowed, though analysts said at the time they weren’t worried about the stock’s slide.

Shares closed Thursday at $160.59, down 1.1%, before the results came out, and were little changed in after-hours trading. The stock is down more than 55% from its 52-week high of $361.40.

The company announced in its 29 October results announcement that it intends to continue to reward STRC with an annual rate of 12%. Dividends are now to be paid via daily dividends with effect from 1 November.

According to Strategy’s November 2 filing, it repurchased approximately 2.09 million STRC shares using its general-purpose “USD Cash” balance.

This would also bring down future payment obligations for the company, as these shares paid dividend; the company had $748.6 million preferred-share repurchase authorisation remaining on its books.

Meanwhile, it raised $164 million by selling approximately 1.18 million new MSTR common shares. Of those proceeds, $65.5 million funded Bitcoin purchases, and $98.5 million went into USD Cash.

The 811 BTC purchase brought Strategy’s holdings to 849,327 BTC. The company paid an average of $80,846 per Bitcoin for the latest additions, including fees and expenses.

From its separate USD Reserve, it also used $43.4 million to pay preferred-stock dividends during the week.

As of November 1, what Strategy held, which supports dividends and debt interest, was $4.79 billion. Its general-purpose USD Cash balance stood at $132.7 million.

#5219. Ripple Partner Reaches One Million People With Safe Water

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple Partner Reaches One Million People With Safe Water

The access to clean water isn’t taken for granted in many jurisdictions across the globe. Water. Org is here to fix it.

Ripple and Water.org are expanding a collaboration that has already helped more than one million people gain access to safe water or sanitation financing across Latin America.

The nonprofit, co-founded by Gary White and Matt Damon, is now layering Ripple Payments, the RLUSD stablecoin, and digital asset custody tools into its operations so capital can move faster and cheaper into emerging markets.

Water.org has used Ripple Payments to move more than $3.2 million across four markets.

Settlement times in Mexico and Brazil dropped from two to three days to same-day, while payment processing became available around the clock instead of being limited by a single daily banking cutoff.

Transaction fees fell by as much as 66 percent, so a larger share of every dollar reaches borrowers rather than intermediaries.

Ripple committed $6 million over three years to support Water.org programs such as WaterCredit, which partners with local financial institutions to offer affordable loans for household taps, toilets, and piped connections.

Finance as a tool to solve the water crisis 💧@Water co-founders Matt Damon and Gary White joined @bgarlinghouse on the Swell main stage to share how Ripple Payments and RLUSD are helping @Water reach more people, faster. pic.twitter.com/VXdttesBK6

Separately, Water.org received a $1.25 million grant in Ripple’s RLUSD through the Stablecoin Impact Fund. That capital is intended to expand stablecoin-enabled WaterCredit disbursements into Indonesia, the Philippines, and Uganda.

Water.org will also begin using Ripple’s Wallet-as-a-Service technology to manage digital assets as the programs scale. Beyond the direct funding, Ripple joined Get Blue, the Water.org movement modeled after the (RED) campaign, as its exclusive digital-asset and fintech partner.

Founding brand partners include Gap, Amazon, Starbucks, and Ecolab. Ripple’s first year of Get Blue support helped reach 400,000 people, with the three-year commitment expected to support 1.2 million as Water.org works toward its broader goal of reaching 200 million people by 2030.

Gary White, co-founder and CEO of Water.org, said the actual water crisis is fundamentally a funding-flow problem rather than a lack of capital, and that Ripple’s infrastructure has shown what efficient movement of money looks like in practice.

Brad Garlinghouse, Ripple’s CEO, noted that the partnership demonstrates the original promise of crypto and blockchain: making money move faster, more efficiently, and globally for real-world needs.

💧🌍 WATER IS LIFE. CRYPTO IS CHANGING THE GAME! 🚀Hollywood superstar Matt Damon in conversation with @bgarlinghouse is helping tackle the global water crisis through https://t.co/AMHUwOVte1, and Ripple is part of a bigger conversation about using financial innovation to… pic.twitter.com/U42l8YvnZM

White and Matt Damon joined Garlinghouse for a fireside chat at Ripple Swell in New York.

The expanded setup combines traditional philanthropic capital with on-chain settlement and custody so that repaid loans can be recycled into new lending through vehicles such as the WaterEquity Everspring Fund.

For Water.org, the practical result is more of each donated or invested dollar reaching families that need household water connections. For Ripple, it is another demonstration of its payments and stablecoin stack operating outside pure trading venues and inside humanitarian finance.

#5218. Solana Officially Scores 1,000 Days Without Outage

The Solana network has hit a significant milestone in its quest to overcome its early hurdles, successfully going 1,000 days without a network-wide outage.

This feat stands in stark contrast to Solana's past, when the blockchain experienced some notable network disruptions. One of the more significant outages occurred in September 2021, when a spike in bot traffic from Grape Protocol IDO transactions led to a surge in transactions that overwhelmed validators and hindered consensus, resulting in a roughly 17-hour network outage.

The Solana network experienced similar problems in April 2022, with a large traffic spike due to an NFT mint that led to a roughly 7-hour outage. Another outage happened in June 2022, when a bug involving durable nonce transactions caused block production to stop for roughly 4.5 hours. Finally, in September 2022, the network experienced a fork due to a bug in the consensus layer, which led to a halt in block production lasting over 6 hours.

The final major outage occurred back in February 2023, when abnormal block forwarding overwhelmed Solana's Turbine block propagation system, leaving validators stuck in a vote-only state and leading to a coordinated restart. This would prove to be a monumental event for Solana in terms of its engineering progress.

Solana has seen a string of updates and engineering innovations by its developers in an effort to improve the network's ability to avoid the failures that had plagued it in the past. Some of these features include stake-weighted quality of service to better prioritize traffic from staked validators. The network also saw networking innovations such as QUIC that provide more flexibility in dealing with spam and congestion. There have also been updates to deduplication logic following the February 2023 outage. Additionally, the network has seen innovations such as a local fee market and other scheduling improvements to discourage users and bots from spamming the network with duplicate transactions.

Recently, Solana has emphasized that network resilience should be taken seriously. In a September 2026 update, the project shared that the network has seen 100% uptime since February 2024 and has continued to handle large amounts of traffic. It also highlighted a major infrastructure provider experiencing a routing failure in August 2026 that caused validators representing nearly 29% of the network's stake to go offline, but this did not result in a halt in block production. The project uses this as an example of increased fault tolerance.

For Solana, this 1,000-day milestone is not just a success in terms of network uptime. It's a statement and a demonstration to the world that a network once mocked for outages can now support serious financial and on-chain use cases.
